subject: Embed runtime + certification discussion — next steps

From: Marta Lopez <marta@shipyardlabs.com>

Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam@shipyardlabs.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T16:12:00-04:00
Subject: Embed runtime partnership — draft term sheet and kickoff

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the intro — really excited about the potential fit between Shipyard and Redwood. Per our call earlier today, attaching a short draft term sheet and a spreadsheet listing the technical checkpoints we expect for an embedded runtime.

Two quick asks to start:
- Can Redwood support a private, air-gapped package for on-prem customers (minimal outbound telemetry)?
- What certification path would you put Shipyard through to qualify for a “Redwood Certified Integrator” program (security, perf, and QA gates)?

I attached: shipyard_draft_term_sheet.pdf and redwood_embed_requirements_v1.xlsx (see summary tab).

Goal: get alignment on commercial guardrails and a certification checklist so we can scope the joint engineering effort and marketing co-branding.

Proposed next step: 30–45 minute follow-up with your product/legal/partnership leads — would you and your team be available next week?

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Head of Partnerships 
Shipyard Labs

Subject: Re: Embed runtime partnership — draft term sheet and kickoff

Hi Marta — thanks for the materials and the clear checklist. Putting Karthik (product), Vanessa (partnerships) on copy to surface the right owners.

Quick answers up front:
1) Private/on-prem package: yes, we can provide a self-contained runtime bundle for air-gapped installs. We typically ship a tarball + install script; we will need to agree on telemetry knobs (defaults: disabled) and an attestable SBOM for compliance.
2) Certified Integrator program: we have a three-tier certification (Validated, Certified, Premier). For an ISV embed like Shipyard I’d expect the Certified track (security review, perf tests at target QPS, integration QA checklist). There is a short commercial addendum for co-branding and referral credits.

Suggested next step: internal sync Thurs 4/14 at 10am PT with Product/Legal/Partner Ops. If that works for you, I’ll send a calendar invite and draft an initial mutual action plan for the meeting.

CC: Karthik — can you prepare a one-page perf/cert matrix and a pointer to the SBOM/telemetry policy?
CC: Vanessa — happy to loop in partner marketing once we have the certification gates.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Embed runtime partnership — draft term sheet and kickoff

Hi Marta / Aisha — looping in on the legal/ops side. A few operational notes from Redwood Legal & Delivery: 

1) Telemetry / Data Flows: we can ship runtime with telemetry disabled by default. However, certain optional features (usage metrics for cost/health) require an opt-in call-home. For certification, Shipyard will need to run our diagnostic suite (local) and provide logs to us under an NDA so we can validate perf gates.

2) Licensing & Escrow: We generally don’t provide production source, but we do offer a limited escrow arrangement for critical adaptors (third-party connectors) under a narrowly scoped escrow agreement and release triggers (bankruptcy, acquisition). We can share standard escrow language; expect redlines from Shipyard Legal.

3) Support SLAs & Pricing: certified partners can buy a partner support bundle (9x5 or 24x7) and get discounted reserved capacity for co-managed customer deployments. Commercial model options: (a) embed fee + revenue share, (b) referral + support fees, (c) OEM enterprise license. We can discuss preferred models and map to Shipyard customer profiles in the call.

I’ll prepare the legal bullets and a draft NDA/escrow addendum for the meeting.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Legal Operations (Redwood Inference)
